newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London little changed, Dow seen off.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London little changed, Dow seen off.

text.p: U.S. shares in London were mostly flat in relatively quiet trade on Tuesday after the Dow see-sawed to a record high overnight.
"Share prices are fairly steady around the closes," said one senior trader. "There's been no real dramatic moves."
In the U.S. on Monday, the Dow added 23 points to 6,567.18, surpassing the previous all-time high of 6,560.91 set on December 27.
Blue chips led the way again with cyclicals also benefitting from the growing perception of strong growth in the economy. Treasuries slipped on fears of higher interest rates ahead.

"The bond is almost unchanged and the futures are slightly lower so I'm looking for a fractionally lower opening in New York," one dealer said. "But who can tell in this market when it moves 50 points one way and then the other."

Among individual share movers, Apple Computer bounced back to be up $1/4 at $18-1/8, after the shares had plunged more than 20 percent in response to expected losses of up to $150 million in the latest quarter.
Boeing was $1/8 higher at $106-3/8, after dealers said Salomon Brothers had repeated a strong "buy" recommendation on the shares.
Shares in Newmont Mining lost $1/4 to $41-1/4 amid talk that U.S. billionaire George Soros had turned negative on the stock.
AT&T shares were $1/8 better at $39-5/8, bouncing back from recent weakness and IBM was off $1/2 at $160-7/8.
Elsewhere Ford was up $1/8 at $33-1/4 after the company reported an 11 percent rise in December sales.
